subject: Model eligibility check & eval next steps — Ledgerly discovery
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@ledgerly.com>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@ledgerly.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Model eligibility check & eval next steps — Ledgerly discovery

Alex / Priya — thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap of what we heard and a proposed, low-friction next step so we can evaluate open-model suitability relative to your current proprietary baseline. Attaching the prompt set you shared in call as a starter (ledgerly_eval_promptset.csv).

High-level read: you care most about (1) domain fidelity on billing & reconciliation instructions, (2) conservative response behavior (avoid hallucination), (3) latency under 200 ms p95 for synchronous flows, and (4) cost targets for 1–3M monthly queries.

Proposed quick eligibility run (spin-up using Redwood hosted sandbox):
- Candidate open models to trial (initial shortlist): OpenX-2.7B-chat, OpenX-13B-chat, OpenTitan-70B-quant.
- Customer baseline for comparison: Ledgerly-prop-v1 (you said a fine-tuned internal checkpoint).
- Evaluation buckets: automated metrics (exact-match / normalized-F1 on canonical answers), hallucination rate (binary adjudication), and a small human preference panel (n=120 domain queries).
- Acceptance / parity thresholds we recommend for an initial gate: 
  * Automated metric drop vs baseline <= 2.0 percentage points absolute (e.g., F1_baseline - F1_open <= 2.0)
  * Human preference: open model within ±5 points of baseline (i.e., not worse by more than 5%)
  * Hallucination rate for safety-critical answer types < 3% absolute and no catastrophic failures on the 20 sanity-check prompts we flagged
  * Latency: p95 under 200 ms (hosted) or p95 under 250 ms for quantized variants if cost savings are material

If an open model meets the gate, next stage is a 10k-query mixed workload evaluation including BPE token-cost analysis and throughput profiling (we’ll include recommended batching & cache knobs).

Immediate asks from your side: please confirm the canonical test set we should use (attached is the promptset you dropped on the call) and whether we have permission to run those queries against the Ledgerly-prop-v1 (you indicated yes but asked for a signed NDA scope — we’ll loop legal if required).

Next internal items (who I cc’d): Monica — can you provision a Redwood sandbox run and seed the dataset? Priyom — can you draft the quick eval harness and the human preference template? Aditya — can you pre-allocate one short burst of Dedicated capacity for the 10k run in case the hosted queueing impacts latency?

Thanks all — I’ll schedule the quick kickoff once Alex confirms test-set & baseline access.

—
Ben Carter
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachments: ledgerly_eval_promptset.csv (CSV prompt + expected_answer stub)
From: Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@ledgerly.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@ledgerly.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:43:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Model eligibility check & eval next steps — Ledgerly discovery

Ben — thanks for the detailed recap. Confirm we want Redwood to run the initial sandboxed comparisons against our Ledgerly-prop-v1; we can provide access to a read-only inference endpoint (no training artifacts). Please only use the attached promptset; the data is redacted for PII.

Couple of clarifications from our side:
- Human preference panel: we can provide 6 domain SMEs to run through the 120 samples you suggested; they prefer a simple A/B blind test with three possible labels (better / same / worse).
- Compliance: results for the sandbox run should be stored in our EU project folder (we have an EU data residency requirement for any customer data replicas). If Redwood needs to run in hosted EU region, let us know.
- Timeline: we’d like the quick signal in the next 10 business days if possible — that will feed an internal gating meeting.

I’ll loop in Legal separately re: the limited-scope access; otherwise proceed.

—
Alex Taylor
Head of ML Platform, Ledgerly
alex.taylor@ledgerly.com
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Model eligibility check & eval next steps — Ledgerly discovery

Internal — Alex confirmed baseline endpoint access and EU residency requirement. Quick ops plan and owner list below (short timeline: 10 business days goal):

Plan (Phase 0 -> Phase 1):
Phase 0 (sandbox quick-run, ~3 business days):
- Monica: provision hosted EU sandbox in Redwood EU region; ensure logs are isolated to Ledgerly EU folder (use retention=30d for the run). Attach: redwood_eval_instructions.md.
- Priyom: implement the quick eval harness (script + instructions) that will run the three open candidates against the provided promptset and the baseline endpoint. Required outputs: automated metric CSV, hallucination flags, latency profile (p50/p95), per-prompt token-cost estimate. Please include an inline field for the model config used (temperature, max_tokens, quantization flags).
- Aditya: reserve a burst node on Dedicated (one GPU V100-equivalent) for the 10k run if the hosted queue introduces jitter; mark as fallback only.

Phase 1 (extended 10k mixed workload, human preference, final readout, ~5 business days):
- Run 10k mixed workload to measure throughput/cost.
- Human panel (Ledgerly SMEs) to label 120 blind A/B samples — Priyom to provide survey link and instructions.
- Produce baseline_comparison_report.pdf with the gate table. Gate table will implement the thresholds we discussed: automated drop <= 2pp; human preference within ±5pp; hallucination < 3%; latency p95 <= 200 ms (or p95<=250ms for quantized if we hit cost savings >20%).

Known risk items / quality flags to watch during Phase 0:
- Hallucination regressions on multi-step billing reconciliation prompts (we should instrument token-level provenance markers).
- Temperature tuning: some open variants show better correctness at lower temperature but may appear terse; plan to sweep temp in {0.0, 0.2, 0.5} for top candidates.
- Tokenization edge cases: Canonical answers include ledger-specific codes that sometimes get split; add a normalization pass to the scoring script.

Deliverables / timeline:
- Phase 0 kickoff today if Monica can provision by EOD — target quick-run results in 3 business days.
- Phase 1 kickoff after quick-run readout; final readout for Alex’s gating meeting within 10 business days.

If you see any blockers, call them out. I’ll put a short calendar for the kickoff and a readout slot.

—
Ben Carter
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Model eligibility check & eval next steps — Ledgerly discovery

Ben / team — noted. I have a couple quick additions to the harness and the scoring so we don’t get false negatives on parity: 

1) Prompt bundle: I’ll add a small set of adversarial paraphrases (~30 prompts) that exercise the hallucination modes we saw on the call — billing edge cases and multi-step reconciliations. Those will be split out in the report so we can see gap by prompt subtype.
2) Human preference survey: will be single-blind with randomized order; will include a separate ‘safety flag’ checkbox so SMEs can mark an output as unacceptable even if it scores well on automated metrics.
3) Aggregation rule: for automated metrics use macro-averaged F1 across intent buckets; don’t let high-volume trivial prompts dominate.

I’ll push the harness to the shared drive and post the run instructions. Monica — ping me when the EU sandbox is ready and I’ll start the quick-run.

—
Priyom Das
Senior ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
